headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dexter’s broad egress and financial-data handling can feed social-auto-upload’s autonomous upload workflow, while shared write/conflict risk is limited by B’s no-write profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can ingest files in .dexter/scratchpad/ and use autonomous execution with broad egress; B can handle media/account workflows but has no filesystem read or MCP. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual file or content transfer, making the blast radius small and the pathway unusual.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-generated content into A’s scratchpad or prompts
IF A is configured to parse untrusted text as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste B outputs into A prompts without review
Use a fixed prompt template for A
Disable any auto-import of files into A
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs; B touches account data and also has broad egress. Even without a shared filesystem, any operator-mediated transfer of A’s outputs into B’s upload flow can expose sensitive data to third parties in default-style usage, so the interaction exists and the blast radius includes sensitive data.
conditions: IF A outputs financial or market data into a file or prompt later consumed by B
IF B uploads content derived from A to a social platform or API
mitigations: Keep financial data out of B inputs
Review A outputs before any upload step
Use redacted summaries instead of raw data
Separate credentials for A and B
requires-engineering: add content-class filters before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while B explicitly cannot write files or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only plausible overlap is operator-managed file handoff, so the conflict surface is narrow and not dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same operator-managed scratch directory
IF B is wrapped by an external process that adds write access
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Keep B read-only at the OS level
Avoid concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Name files with agent-specific prefixes
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is autonomous and can generate market or financial outputs that B may then package or upload. B has no built-in verification surface in the profile, so if A’s output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect public posts or account actions. The pathway is inferred from A’s autonomous execution and B’s upload role, not directly documented.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text, captions, or metadata without human review
IF A’s outputs are forwarded into B’s publishing workflow
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B publishes
Require source links for any factual claim from A
Use a checklist for post content validation
Limit B to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before upload

E_compliance.rationale: A handles financial and market data and requests multiple API keys; B handles account data and uploads to social platforms. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different sensitive data classes and external services, so compliance risk exists through retention and logging differences. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF regulated financial data from A is forwarded into B’s account workflows
IF either agent logs or retains shared data longer than policy allows
mitigations: Minimize shared data to what is necessary
Review retention settings for both tools
Avoid sending regulated data to social upload workflows
Separate audit logs by agent
requires-engineering: document a data-flow and retention matrix
